steps.text: Try the clock: press Space to pause, then 1, 2 or 3 for speed
steps.why: The game runs at 1× from the start: one day takes about 72 seconds. Pause whenever you want to think; nothing happens while paused.

steps.text: Click a building on the map
steps.why: The card shows how dangerous it is, how far, and what may still be inside.

steps.text: Plan a scavenging trip to a house or shop
steps.why: Water, food and medicine only come from searching buildings. Pick Plan a trip on the building card.

steps.text: Put someone on Guard for the night shift
steps.why: Open the People tab and drag a name onto Guard in the Night column.

steps.text: Open the Stores tab and look at your water and food
steps.why: These are what you are really playing against. Days left is shown for each.

start.text: Your five survivors are in the house with the blue outline. Time is already running: Space pauses, 1, 2 and 3 change the speed. The Getting started list on the map walks you through the first day. Press H at any time for the full guide.

speed.text: Space pauses, 1, 2 and 3 change the speed. The game stops by itself when something needs a decision, so it is safe to speed up. Your goal: keep anyone in the group alive until 06:00 on Day 30.

building.text: This card shows what you know about the building: danger (infected trapped inside), how far it is, and what was left when someone last looked. Plan a trip to send one person to search it. Move base makes it your new home.

planner.text: Pick who goes, and when. Midday heat keeps infected sluggish; night is far more dangerous. The risk and the times shown are estimates of exactly what the simulation will do. Nothing starts until you press Send.

first_trip.text: Someone is on the road. Trips take hours, and the group cannot reach them. You will hear when they return; the Log tab shows what they found and what happened on the way.

trip_back.text: A trip has ended. The Stores tab shows what came back. Anything searched is gone from the building for good, and other survivors strip the shops too, so waiting costs you.

first_night.text: Night has fallen. Infected are most active now. Put someone on Guard for the night shift (People tab, job board) and keep noise down: hammering and generators draw them.

first_water.text: The taps are about to fail. Put someone on Collect water now to fill every container, then keep an eye on water days in the Stores tab. Afterwards, water must be fetched and boiled.

taps_failed.text: The taps have failed. Water now comes from tanks, rain or the canal, and must be boiled before it is safe. Check the Base tab's orders (policies) and the Stores tab for how many days you have.

power_out.text: The grid is down. Fridges stop and the nights are dark. A generator gives light at the cost of fuel and noise; set it in the Base tab if you have one.

first_decision.text: A decision is waiting. The game pauses for these. Each option says what will follow; options marked 'can't be undone' are final. Decide later keeps it in the Alerts list.

first_bite.text: Someone has been bitten. A bite is not always the end of the story, but the fever comes fast. Keep them apart (quarantine), treat them, and read every option in the decision window before you pick.

first_wound.text: A wound has gone bad. Put someone with medical skill on the Treat job, and use antibiotics if you have them. Untreated, an infection becomes a fever and then sepsis.

first_illness.text: Someone is ill. Rest, water and rehydration salts help. An ill person should not scavenge or guard.

first_attack.text: The base was attacked. Defense comes from barricades, guards and strong walls. Put someone on Fortify (it uses materials), and keep attention low: noise, light and smell all raise it.

breach.text: The defenses were breached. Check on everyone in the People tab. Consider more barricades, a guard, or moving to a stronger building.

first_death.text: Someone has died. You win by keeping anyone alive, so the group carries on. Watch for stress in the others: people who see too much may refuse to work or leave.

joined.text: A stranger has joined the group. One more mouth to feed, but also one more pair of hands. Give them a job in the People tab.

food_spoiled.text: Food has spoiled in the heat. Fridges need power; cooked food does not keep. Eat perishables first and put someone on the Cook job.

noise.text: Noise drew infected to the base. Hammering, generators, gunfire and forcing doors all carry. The Noise overlay on the map shows where it spreads.

tab_people.text: People: the job board on top (drag a name to a job for the Day and Night shifts) and a card for each survivor with water, food, sleep and stress meters. Click a card for the full picture. Hover any number to see why it is what it is.

tab_stores.text: Stores: everything the group owns, in real units (litres, kcal, kg). Water and food show days left at the current pace. Rations and boiling are set in the Base tab.

tab_base.text: Base: defense against attacks, how much attention the base draws, and standing orders such as rations, boiling water, the generator and firearms. High attention means attacks are coming.

tab_log.text: Log: the story so far, newest at the bottom. Click an entry to jump to where it happened.

tab_stats.text: Stats: one chart per resource, one point per day. Falling lines are your early warning.

overlay.text: Map layers: Infected shows estimated infected per zone; Noise, Light and Smell show what draws them; Attention is how much the base is noticed. What you see is what the group has observed, not always the truth.

alerts.text: The Alerts button lists everything that needs attention now, worst first. Click an alert to jump to the right place. Which ones pause the game is set in Menu, Settings.

day3.text: Day 3. The first days are about water, food and getting a routine: guard at night, scavenging at dawn or dusk, cooking, resting. From here the town gets worse every week: power, taps and the heat. Plan ahead.

day10.text: Day 10. Nearby buildings are picked over. Longer trips mean more risk. Consider whether to stay and fortify, or move to a better building (click it, Move base).

day25.text: Five days to go. You win at 06:00 on Day 30 if anyone is still alive. Spend what you have kept for later.

guide.title: The goal
guide.body:
The infected are sick living people, not the undead. You lead a small group in a town after an outbreak. You win by keeping anyone alive in the group until 06:00 on Day 30.

You never walk anyone around. You give people jobs, send them on trips, set standing orders and make the hard calls. The world keeps going whether you look or not: the power and taps fail, the heat climbs and other survivors strip the shops.

guide.title: Time
guide.body:
A run starts at 1× and the clock stops whenever you press Space. 1, 2 and 3 set the speed: one day takes about 72 seconds at 1×, a third of that at 3×, and about 7 seconds at 10×.

The game stops by itself when a decision is waiting and for the alerts you choose in Menu, Settings, so speeding up is safe. Esc opens the menu to save, load or change settings.

guide.title: The map
guide.body:
Click a building to see its card: how dangerous it is, how far, and what is left. From the card you can plan a scavenging trip or move your base there.

The Show buttons switch map layers: infected, noise, light, smell, attention and disease. Mouse wheel zooms, drag pans. Dark areas are places the group has not seen lately: you see what the group has observed, not always the truth.

guide.title: People and jobs
guide.body:
The People tab has a job board: one row per job, one column for the day shift (06-18) and one for the night shift (18-06). Drag a name onto a cell. Everyone needs sleep, so a person on a day job should rest at night.

Useful jobs: Guard (night defense), Fortify (barricades from materials), Collect water, Cook, Treat (medicine) and Rest. Hover a job's name for what it does. Warnings under the board flag unwise assignments.

guide.title: Scavenging
guide.body:
Water, food, fuel and medicine come from searching buildings. Pick a building, then Plan a trip. The planner shows how long it takes, the chance of getting hurt, and the loot you can hope for.

Midday heat makes infected sluggish but wears people down. Dusk and night are far more dangerous. Loot is finite: what you take, or other survivors take, is gone.

guide.title: Stores and survival
guide.body:
Water is in litres, food in kcal, fuel in litres. Each person needs about 3 litres of water and 2,000 kcal a day, more in the heat. The Stores tab shows days left; hover for what makes it up.

When the taps fail, water has to be fetched from tanks, rain or the canal, and boiled. Raw rice, lentils and flour need the Cook job.

guide.title: The base
guide.body:
The Base tab shows defense and attention. Barricades and guards raise defense. Noise, light and smell raise attention: when it is high, infected come in numbers. Hammering, generators and gunfire are loud.

If the place gets too dangerous, move. A new building starts with fewer barricades but less attention. Standing orders (rations, boiling, generator, firearms) are set here too.

guide.title: Bodies and minds
guide.body:
Each survivor has four meters: water, food, sleep and stress. Heat, wounds and fear all take their toll. Wounds can become infected; a bite starts a fever that ends in turning unless it can be treated. Stressed people refuse to work, and may leave the group.

The Alerts button lists what needs attention now. Decisions pause the game and show what each option will lead to.

guide.title: Tips for the first days
guide.body:
1. Collect water before the taps fail, and fill every container.
2. Put someone on Guard every night.
3. Scavenge at dawn or dusk, not at night.
4. Search houses first: low danger, and rice and lentils.
5. Keep medicine for the wounded; infections kill.
6. Do not hammer or run a generator unless you have to.
7. Rest people. A tired group makes mistakes.

This guide is always on H, and the hints can be turned on again in Menu, Settings.
